scope: Replace the public RM65 folding replay with a visible-axis-constrained, branch-continuous IK result and correct the left AG2F90-C tool roll.
summary: The eight-second dual-RM65 replay now follows the source-visible gripper axes without the prior joint-limit wrist flip, and both AG2F90-C opening planes remain parallel to the tabletop through an explicit left 90-degree tool-roll regularizer.
evidence: The H.264 comparison is 2048x768, 24 FPS, 192 frames and 8.0 seconds with SHA-256 7241c97a72948ea1e468ee843bf73b0df82ccc8d3f5e22393a0269d38144ca3d.
All 192 saved states are finite. Mean left/right rendered EEF FK residual is 0.7234/0.6789 mm and maximum residual is 3.7761/1.9191 mm.
Mean source-visible gripper-axis error is 3.7743 degrees on the left and 1.4645 degrees on the right; maxima are 7.5497 and 3.0823 degrees.
The previous joint-4 wrist-flip branch reached approximately +/-3.106 rad. V16 joint-4 ranges are -0.0577 to 0.3653 rad on the left and 1.0464 to 1.7597 rad on the right.
The minimum margin to any RM65 joint limit is 0.2704 rad, and the fixed left tool-roll offset is +90 degrees.
The comparison, simulation-only render, poster and state NPZ are bound by SHA-256 in the public v16 audit.
lessons: A monocular EEF point does not determine full wrist SO(3); forcing a synthetic full orientation can select a position-equivalent but visibly wrong wrist branch.
Constraining only the visible wrist-to-tip axis, then selecting a continuous path over multistart IK candidates, resolves elbow and wrist posture without changing the EEF motion.
An exact 90-degree discrepancy around the gripper axis is more consistent with a missing flange-to-tool transform than a link-length or RM65 URDF error.
limitations: The source-image axes and camera-depth components are reviewed RGB constraints, not calibrated metric pose measurements.
The +90-degree tool roll is a visual/tool-frame regularizer; hardware deployment requires measurement of the physical flange-to-gripper transform.
The result remains a kinematic replay without deformable cloth dynamics, enabled collision proof, force closure, controller validation or recorded real-robot execution.
next_actions: Move the tool-roll correction from a replay offset into a calibrated flange-to-gripper transform before hardware control.
Automate wrist-axis and robot-base estimation with reconstruction-conditioned evaluators while preserving the published joint-limit and FK gates.
